findings.description: [demoted to minor: no concrete failure scenario, so it cannot gate; reported as major by the reviewer] contracts/web-endpoints.md lists the Data section (delete cached media and events now) as risky: it requires a sign-in under 5 minutes old plus a typed confirmation. The implemented media-delete route only checks origin, session, form token and a checkbox-supplied literal confirm=delete. It never calls #fresh(session), which #approval does call, and the page offers a checkbox instead of typed text. Anyone using a still-open owner session can irreversibly delete cached media for every household without re-authenticating. The admin-page test submits confirm=delete and does not exercise a stale sign-in. The contract scheduled this section for iteration 004, but the operation ships now without its control. Check #fresh before deletion, require typed confirmation, and test a stale session.
findings.title: Delete-now for all cached media lacks the required fresh sign-in and typed confirmation

findings.description: [demoted to minor: no concrete failure scenario, so it cannot gate; reported as major by the reviewer] The recorded owner decision says withdrawal denies the next GET or Range request and that an already authorized transfer may finish; plan.md Notes says a transfer already authorized can finish while each subsequent GET or Range must recheck. MediaHandoff.read calls authorize for every 256 KiB chunk, and authorize requires the ticket expires_at to be in the future and the current policy and approval generations to match. After the 200/206 headers and Content-Length have been sent, withdrawal, a sound or camera setting change, or simply reaching the five-minute grant expiry makes pull() reject and truncates the response. A slow receiver that starts a clip of up to 32 MiB shortly before expiry therefore receives a broken download although its GET was authorized in time. No design amendment was found in the iteration 003 records inspected; quality-evidence.md only describes the new behavior. Authorize once per request and let that response finish, or obtain and record an owner decision for the changed semantics. Add a multi-chunk test covering expiry and withdrawal after headers.
findings.title: Per-chunk grant checks abort transfers the approved design allows to finish

findings.description: The catch that records denied fetches and logs media_download_failed covers only work before the Response is returned. Later chunks run in ReadableStream.pull without error handling there. A MediaDenied, storage failure, short read or 30-second timeout on a later chunk errors the stream, but mediaDownload writes no denied audit row and no operational log. The access log shows only the initial allowed fetch, so an operator cannot distinguish a truncated or revoked delivery from a complete one. Handle errors in pull: audit denials and log other failures with the item identifier before erroring the stream.
findings.title: Failures after the first chunk are neither audited as denied nor logged by the download handler

findings.description: After authorize succeeds, an invalid byte range returns 416 with the item length in Content-Range, without calling auditFetch. The allowed audit is written only inside media.read for the first chunk. An authenticated receiver can thus confirm a live grant and learn the item size with no media-access entry, unlike the denied paths for known items. The same branch rejects multi-range and syntactically invalid Range headers with 416 rather than serving the full representation. Record the outcome before returning 416.
findings.title: Authorized requests with an unsatisfiable or unsupported range leave no access record

summary: Static risk-based review of the iteration 003 media handoff: staging, item grants, receiver downloads, approvals, audit, admin settings and deletion, OAuth scope gating, Blob/file storage, migrations and pilot media fetching. Two contract violations: deleting all cached media skips the required recent sign-in and typed confirmation, and an authorized transfer is cut off by withdrawal or grant expiry between chunks although the owner-approved decision lets it finish. Two minor findings cover unobserved mid-stream failures and unaudited invalid-range or chunk reads. Not inspected in depth: connector internals, CI, unrelated infrastructure. No tests were run by the reviewer; the only controller verification command was the governance validator, which exited 0. Planned tasks not yet implemented were not treated as defects.
